description: The internal URL/filter structure of bank.gov.ua/ua/legislation (act-type filters, date filters, pagination, per-act permalink pattern) could not be enumerated because the page 403'd.

Non-bank / payment-service-provider normative base was only identified via an NBU news announcement; the actual section URL and its taxonomy were not confirmed. Given sector=both this is a material hole.

Adjacent Ukrainian actors that shape or mirror NBU prudential deadlines were not explored in this cell (Ministry of Justice act-registration register, Deposit Guarantee Fund, Verkhovna Rada finance committee, EU-approximation reporting). Some sit outside this cell by design but the boundary should be explicit.
Historical depth was not tested: whether bank.gov.ua exposes pre-2019 acts or whether zakon.rada's 4,176-document NBU set is complete back to 1991 was not verified document-by-document.
Russian-language mirrors of NBU acts exist on zakon.rada (uk-ru paths) but were not assessed; run languages are uk/en so this is deliberate, though ru mirrors sometimes have different availability.

No archive or index of CLOSED consultations was located. The tagged news stream is chronological and the drafts_discussion items age out of the visible list; there is no year-scoped consultation register comparable to the Ministry of Finance's 'Проекти регуляторних актів для обговорення у 2026 р.'.

Comment deadlines exist only as free Ukrainian prose inside the article body ('Зауваження та пропозиції ... приймаються ... до 04 вересня 2026 року включно'), with Ukrainian month names and occasional variants ('до <date> включно', 'протягом ... днів'). There is no machine-readable deadline field anywhere.

The banking association (НАБУ) and the payments association (ЕМА) were identified, but no verified source was obtained for the finance-companies, insurance, credit-union or leasing associations that respond to the large non-bank share of NBU consultations.

The English mirror of the consultation feed returned fewer items than the Ukrainian one (7 vs 10 detail links in the same probe), and the substantive attachments (проєкт постанови, аналіз впливу, порівняльна таблиця) are Ukrainian-only.

Every high-value host in this cell (bank.gov.ua, drs.gov.ua, mof.gov.ua, kmu.gov.ua) is bot-defended to some degree, and nabu.ua rate-limits. Plain HTTP fetching is not a sufficient collection technology for this cell.

The link between a Verkhovna Rada bill and the NBU sub-legislation it triggers is not yet mapped; the Rada portal was identified but no keyword/committee filter was validated for banking and payments bills.

The cell's confirmed adviser set is roughly a dozen firms; second-tier and boutique fintech/payments advisers (Aequo, Redcliffe Partners, Ilyashev, Eterna, Axon Partners, Juscutum and similar fintech-leaning boutiques) are unconfirmed. Boutiques are often faster than the majors on payment-institution licensing detail.

Advisers increasingly push first-look commentary to LinkedIn and Telegram (a FinTech Ukraine Telegram channel surfaced during searching) before the firm website is updated. These channels were not systematically explored in this run.

Confirmed adviser sources are strongest AFTER a rule is adopted. Coverage of the consultation/draft stage (проєкт постанови, громадське обговорення) rests mainly on one trade outlet (dtkt.ua) and occasional firm previews.

Older Baker McKenzie Ukraine legal alerts were only reachable via a third-party repost (USUBC), suggesting firm sites prune historical alerts. No firm was observed to offer a complete dated archive or RSS feed.
The two highest-yield pointers (Lexology, Mondaq) and LIGA360 are all wall-protected to some degree, and all firm content is copyrighted client-alert material.

NSSMC (НКЦПФР, securities/capital markets regulator) was not directly scouted, although capital-markets acquis (MiFID II/MiFIR, CSDR, prospectus) is a large part of Chapter 9 and is named in Commission recommendations.
Consultation venues on the EU side (EBA/ESMA/EIOPA public consultations, Commission calls for evidence via 'Have your say') were not scouted for Ukraine-relevant items.

Ukrainian-language coverage of EU-side bodies (EPC, EBA, ECB) is essentially nil — these publish only in en/EU official languages, so uk searching cannot reach them; conversely EU-side Ukrainian translations of screening material were not found.

No structured, machine-readable register of 'EU directive -> Ukrainian transposition instrument -> deadline' was located; the information is dispersed across AA annexes, pulse.kmu.gov.ua, Ukraine Facility indicators and the annual SWD.
Council of the EU document register (register.consilium.europa.eu), where Association Council/Committee documents and negotiating frameworks are filed, was not queried.
Egmont Group, the EU AMLA (new EU AML Authority) and the EU AML package's implications for a candidate country were not explored, though they will shape Ukraine's AML obligations alongside MONEYVAL.

The IMF Technical Memorandum of Understanding and the quantitative/continuous performance criteria (as opposed to structural benchmarks) were not separately located, nor were IMF technical assistance reports on NBU supervision.
IFC, EIB and bilateral donor (USAID/UK) financial-sector conditionality and technical assistance to the NBU were not covered.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed reachable; all are search-derived and some (Ukraine Facility portal, MoF memorandum section, EBRD project pages) may have moved or been restructured.
Russian-language coverage of the same assessor documents (still widely used by some Ukrainian financial media and by regional AML analysts) was out of scope and not searched.

No Ukrainian banking-association or industry-body media channel (EMA — Ukrainian Interbank Association of Payment Systems Members; NABU/Independent Association of Banks of Ukraine) was captured as its own source, although EMA's director is a recurring quoted voice in the trade press found here.
Ukrainian financial journalism is heavily Telegram-distributed; only one Telegram channel (UAFIC) was identified in this run.
RSS/Atom availability was not established for any candidate; several niche outlets (finbalance.com.ua, banker.ua) may lack machine-readable feeds.
Interfax-Ukraine's banking product, Forbes Ukraine premium and parts of Mind.ua are commercial; the run did not establish subscription terms or whether systematic collection is licensable.
Only Kyiv-centred national outlets were found; no regional or niche B2B payments outlets (e.g. retail/merchant-facing trade media reporting acquiring cost changes) were identified.

Spoken content (conference panels, briefing Q&A, webinars) is the defining medium of this cell but is not text-searchable. Only NBU press briefings have reliable video; association and commercial conferences rarely publish recordings.

No source was found that systematically tracks which NBU official owns which forthcoming rule. Names surfaced only incidentally (Serhii Kholod — payment market regulation; Andriy Podderiogin — Director, Department of Payment Systems and Innovation Development; Yuriy Heletiy — FX/business dialogue; Serhiy Nikolaychuk — First Deputy Governor, international; Oleksii Shaban — payments; Yaroslav Matuzka).

Discovered sources skew to banking and payments/fintech. The non-bank financial services side supervised by the NBU since split-regulation (insurers, credit unions, pawnshops, finance companies) has its own event and association circuit that was not covered in this cell's searches, despite being explicitly affected by the payment-controls draft found here.

LinkedIn and Facebook posts by NBU officials and association staff — a heavily used channel in this market for commenting on forthcoming rules — were not systematically explored. Facebook pages for NABU, AUB, UAFIC and PaySpace were seen only as search artefacts.

No forward-looking master calendar of Ukrainian banking/fintech events exists among the discovered sources; events were found retrospectively via recaps. Only the NBU monetary-policy schedule provides genuine lead time.
Russian-language sources were not searched, though a meaningful share of Ukrainian financial trade commentary and event coverage historically appeared in Russian and some archives remain bilingual.

Two landing URLs were inferred rather than directly observed: the Supreme Court practice-review index and the NBU consumer-protection report index. Individual PDFs under them were observed in search results, but the index paths themselves were not fetched in this run.
Only aggregated PDF complaint statistics were found; no open-data (CSV/API) release of NBU complaint counts by institution was located, and data.gov.ua was not searched in this run.

Administrative-court practice specifically on banks/PSPs challenging NBU enforcement measures (a direct read on where supervision is legally fragile) was not isolated; the commercial-court digest search returned only generic reviews.

The Deposit Guarantee Fund (Фонд гарантування вкладів фізичних осіб) complaint/depositor-dispute stream and the Business Ombudsman Council were not searched in this run, though both publish dispute-outcome material touching banks.

The cell's 'consultations' topic was only reached indirectly (rule-change announcements). A dedicated NBU public-consultation / draft-regulation page for conduct rules was not confirmed, partly because bank.gov.ua blocked fetching.
No supervisory-enforcement source located: NBU sanctions, fines, licence revocations or corrective measures against payment service providers.
E-money specifically (установи електронних грошей, випуск електронних грошей, реєстр емітентів) was reached only through general PSD2/EMD framing, not through a dedicated NBU e-money rulebook page.
Card scheme and national payment system layer (НПС ПРОСТІР, Mastercard/Visa Ukraine local rules, interchange caps) was not covered in this run.
Wartime-specific NBU payment restrictions (currency/payment operation limits under martial law) that overlay the normal PSP rulebook were not scouted.

Plenary stenograms (стенограми пленарних засідань) and roll-call vote records were not individually profiled, though the meetings/zal datasets point at them. Debate text often reveals the political viability of a banking bill before the vote.

Only the Finance/Tax/Customs committee was profiled as lead. Banking and payments bills are regularly co-executed by the European Integration committee (EU-approximation conclusions, directly relevant to PSD2/EMD alignment deadlines) and the Anti-corruption committee (mandatory expert assessment).

Adjacent primary-legislation topics that sit at the edge of banking/payments — virtual assets (віртуальні активи), financial monitoring/AML (фінансовий моніторинг), consumer lending (споживче кредитування), deposit guarantee (ФГВФО) — were not searched as separate keyword families.
The itd.rada.gov.ua search form is an ASP.NET postback form; whether it supports stable GET-parameter queries (needed for reproducible automated searches) was not established.

Public-discussion/consultation surfaces attached to draft laws (committee 'обговорення проєктів законів', committee and parliamentary hearings, working-group announcements) were seen in the committee site navigation but not profiled as distinct sources.

I identified several candidate carriers of the official publication date (zakon.rada b19 index, act cards' 'Опублiковано' field, reestrnpa 'Опублікування в офіційних виданнях'), but did not confirm end-to-end which one gives a reliably complete, machine-parseable date for CMU resolutions and MinFin orders specifically.
MinFin's own 'проєкти регуляторних актів' / 'громадське обговорення' page was not directly located in this run — I confirmed the pattern only on Мінекономіки and МОН.

MinFin acts as shareholder of the state banks, but the corresponding corporate-side disclosures (Ощадбанк, Укрексімбанк, Укргазбанк, Приватбанк supervisory board and governance announcements) were not scouted here — they sit at the edge of this cell and may belong to another.

Decrees of the President (укази Президента України) are also published in the gazette and can bear on financial-sector governance and martial-law-era payment measures, but the president.gov.ua act channel was not scouted in this run.

Wartime practice may alter normal publication and entry-into-force rules (e.g. acts entering force on the day of publication on the government portal rather than gazette issue). I did not verify whether such deviations are currently in effect.
The licensing and redistribution terms of the paid «Офіційний вісник України» online/CD editions from ДП «Українська правова інформація» were not obtained.
Sanctions-enforcement and asset-freeze obligations (NAZK/RNBO/Мінфін sanctions lists) that bind the same AML compliance function were not scouted in this cell.
No verified machine-readable feed (RSS/API) was identified for NSSMC, AMCU or SFMS decision streams; all candidates assume HTML scraping.
No consolidated compliance-deadline calendar for non-NBU supervisors was found; entry-into-force dates are scattered across individual acts and news posts.
AMCU and SFMS have far thinner English coverage than NSSMC; English-only monitoring would miss most concentration decisions and all AML form changes.
Few indirect 'reveals-by-side-effect' sources were captured — e.g. bank annual reports/prospectuses disclosing pending AMCU or SFMS proceedings, or MONEYVAL/FATF evaluation follow-ups.

Ministry of Digital Transformation (Мінцифра) and the Cyber Police Department (Кіберполіція, cyberpolice.gov.ua) were not searched directly in this pass, despite being named in the cell rationale and being the publishers of data-governance and cyber-fraud enforcement material touching PSPs.

Sectoral security profile for the financial sector (галузевий профіль безпеки) — the concrete instrument that will impose technical baselines with dates on banks — has not yet been located as a published document.
No structured change-tracking/alerting service (e.g. LIGA:ZAKON or Verkhovna Rada subscription feeds) was evaluated for automated deadline extraction.
Russian-language Ukrainian legal/trade coverage (still common on some professional portals) was not searched; the run scope specifies uk and en only.
The Register of Payment Infrastructure has a confirmed landing page but no confirmed machine-readable artefact (file or API endpoint).
bank.gov.ua — the single most important domain for this cell — is not fetchable by the plain fetch tooling used here.
E-money issuers, payment-infrastructure service operators and card/processing schemes were not confirmed as separately enumerable populations.
No RSS/Atom or webhook feed was confirmed for NBU register changes or licence-grant announcements.
Reuse terms for the commercial aggregators (YouControl, Opendatabot, Clarity Project) and for OpenSanctions were not read in detail.
Time-series of the regulated population (who held a licence when) is not addressed by any current register surface, which shows present state only.
Український кредитно-банківський союз (UKBS) — one of the four brief-named actors — has no characterised primary source because its domain did not resolve.
NABU's 'Вихідні листи' archive — the actual consultation submissions — was never opened; only its existence and title are known.
Member lists for NABU, AUB, EMA and UAFIC were identified as pages but not actually pulled, so the private-bank / PSP ecosystem map the cell rationale calls for does not yet exist.

The Open API Group participant list surfaced further self-regulatory bodies not in the cell brief and not yet scouted: НАКСУ (credit unions), Blockchain Association of Ukraine, and the insurance association (НАСУ). VAFK was picked up; the others were not.

English-language association output was found only for AUB (full /en/ mirror) and via foreign intermediaries (USUBC, Lexology, PwC, Chambers). NABU, EMA, UAFIC and VAFK were only observed publishing in uk (and ru for NABU/EMA legacy).
Archive depth is unknown for every association source; the NABU monitoring slug series reaches at least -74 and EMA dossiers span 2002-2024, but no start dates or retention policies were confirmed.
No source was found that links a specific NBU draft resolution to the specific association responses it received — the regulator-side and association-side records are separate.
Sense Bank, Kredobank, Credit Agricole Ukraine, A-Bank, ProCredit Bank Ukraine and Pravex were not individually searched in this pass; their notice pages likely mirror the PUMB/OTP patterns.
In-app and push notifications (monobank app, Privat24, OTP Viber/Telegram) are where many customers actually receive terms-change notices; these are not web-observable.
No archival strategy identified for superseded terms versions; banks overwrite PDFs at stable URLs (Oschadbank, Raiffeisen), so historical implementation timing may already be lost.
English-language equivalents exist only sporadically (Oschadbank /en/news, en.otpbank.com.ua) and typically omit the terms-change notices published in Ukrainian.
Bank-side responses to NBU consultations (comments on draft resolutions) were not located as a public artefact from any individual bank; only the NABU association channel hints at this activity.
